paper_sections.title: Salience Network Activity in Perceptual Decisions.
Abstract
paper_sections.parent_section: Salience Network Activity in Perceptual Decisions.

description.value: The study examined salience-network activity and directed functional connectivity between the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex and anterior insulae during four perceptual decision-making tasks with varying sensory difficulty.

spans.text: During four PDM tasks (1) face-house discrimination, (2) happy-angry face discrimination, (3) audiovisual asynchrony and synchrony perception, and a (4) random dot motion direction task, we varied the task difficulty and examined the interactions between these SN nodes.

design.value: Participants completed four perceptual decision-making tasks involving visual or audiovisual stimuli, with task difficulty varied by sensory noise or audiovisual asynchrony; BOLD fMRI and behavioral performance were measured, and brain activity and directed functional connectivity were analyzed.

spans.text: In this study, participants underwent functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) while completing four PDM tasks: (1) face-house discrimination, (2) happy-angry face discrimination, (3) audiovisual asynchrony/synchrony perception, and a (4) random dot motion (RDM) direction task.
We manipulated task difficulty level by mixing red and green dots in our RDM.

source_definition.value: Noise level, ambiguity, or coherence condition used to vary perceptual difficulty.

spans.text: The rationale of difficulty manipulation is to examine how the noise level in stimuli influences nodal activity and network interactions among the nodes of SN.
We regarded detecting asynchrony and synchrony as two-task difficulty levels.
Our interest was to find out how the causal interactions changed due to increased noise level in stimuli, which increased the task difficulty level.
The six motion parameters were entered as nuisance covariates and were regressed out of the data.

Experiment 1: face-house discrimination task

task_description.value: Participants discriminated faces from houses presented with 0%, 40%, or 55% image noise.

spans.text: There were three noise-level conditions and each condition was repeated 60 times (30 times each for faces and houses) in a random order, generating 180 trials in total.
Stimuli were presented in a random order as in an event-related design within each run.

sets.text: The stimulus software presentation (www.neurobs.com) was used to display stimuli and to randomize task trial sequences.

instructions.value: Participants indicated their decisions as quickly and as accurately as possible.

sets.text: indicated their decisions as quickly and as accurately as possible by left/right mouse clicks

stimuli.value: 14 images of faces and 14 images of houses, equalized for luminance and degraded with pixel phase randomization and Gaussian noise.
